pr_title: hostNetwork tests can't share the same port
pr_body:
The pods using hostNetwork use the host network namespace, hence
they have to share it with the rest of the process and pods.
If several pods try to bind to the same port, the test will fail,
so we try to use a non common port, and run the different scenario
in the same test, so we only have to bind once and we avoid consuming
ports reducing the port collision risk.

/kind failing-test
/kind flake
Fixes #104406

```release-note
NONE
```

issue_context.title: hostNetwork tests can't use the same port or they will collide
issue_context.body:
Failed here
```
Kubernetes e2e suite: [sig-network] Services should respect internalTrafficPolicy=Local Pod to Pod (hostNetwork: true) [Feature:ServiceInternalTrafficPolicy] expand_more
```
https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/104401/pull-kubernetes-e2e-ubuntu-gce-network-policies/1427400844852072448
/retest

_Originally posted by @aojea in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/104401#issuecomment-900063266_


This fails because the pod tries to bind port 80, that is a very demanded port, but there are two tests doing that, that increase the chance to collide

review_comments: I think a random port number is best here

we discussed that approach before and that was discarded because the test failures will be hard to debug, you can't know which port is free in advance, at least, with this  approach you know that if it fails to bind it will fail consistently in the same port
This is not great, but the alternative is not much better
